claims.claim: The aggregation and compaction of cells was highly efficient (100%; n = ~1500 from 54 independent experiments).
claims.source: The aggregation and compaction of cells was highly efficient (100%; n = ~1500 from 54 independent experiments) and resulted in a smooth and compacted morphology by day 1 (Figure 1c; Video 1).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from experiments shown in Figure 1c and Video 1.

claims.claim: The potential of blastomeres to form aggregates was restricted to the blastula stage (1000–2000 cells).
claims.source: The potential of blastomeres to form aggregates was restricted to the blastula stage (1000–2000 cells) and cells derived from earlier developmental stages such as early and late morula failed to form stable aggregates or aggregated only partially (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The exact time point of cell dissociation plays a decisive role for the success and efficiency of aggregation.
claims.source: Thus, the exact time point of cell dissociation plays a decisive role for the success and efficiency of aggregation.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observation that only blastula-stage cells efficiently aggregate.

claims.claim: After 1 day of culture, aggregates formed an organized and layered epithelium surrounding the aggregate from day 2 onward.
claims.source: After 1 day of culture, media were supplemented with 2% Matrigel (Figure 1b). The aggregates then formed an organized and layered epithelium surrounding the aggregate from day 2 onward (Figure 1c)
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 1c.

claims.claim: Cells of the peripheral layer expressed neuroepithelial markers N-cadherin and acetylated tubulin, indicating that cells adopted neuroepithelial identity.
claims.source: and the cells of the peripheral layer expressed neuroepithelial markers, for example, N-cadherin and acetylated tubulin, indicating that cells adopted neuroepithelial identity (Figure 1d, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 1d and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: All Rx3::H2B-GFP aggregates started expressing GFP at 15.5 ± 0.36 hpa (n = 17).
claims.source: All aggregates started expressing GFP at 15.5 ± 0.36 hpa (n = 17)
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claims.claim: GFP expression in control Rx3::H2B-GFP embryos started at 13.5 ± 1.03 hr (n = 6) after the blastula stage.
claims.source: with GFP expression in control Rx3::H2B-GFP embryos starting at 13.5 ± 1.03 hr (n = 6) after the blastula stage (Figure 2c), corresponding to the onset of Rx3 expression at around 20 hrs post-fertilization (hpf) (Loosli et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from time-lapse imaging experiments shown in Figure 2c.

claims.claim: In comparison to the embryo, the organoids showed a delay of GFP expression of approximately 2–3 hr which corresponds to the time of re-aggregation.
claims.source: In comparison to the embryo, the organoids showed a delay of GFP expression of approximately 2–3 hr which corresponds to the time of re-aggregation (Video 1).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the timing data between embryos and organoids.

claims.claim: The re-aggregation of primary embryonic pluripotent cells results in an efficient acquisition of retinal fate.
claims.source: This data shows that following our protocol, the re-aggregation of primary embryonic pluripotent cells results in an efficient acquisition of retinal fate.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the GFP expression data in Rx3::H2B-GFP organoids.

claims.claim: Individual blastula-stage cells gave rise to GFP-expressing clones, showing that cells acquire retinal fate autonomously.
claims.source: Also under those conditions, individual cells gave rise to GFP-expressing clones, showing that cells acquire retinal fate autonomously.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from single cell culture experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1c and Video 3.

claims.claim: Single cell-derived clones started to express GFP at about 16 hr.
claims.source: Similar to GFP expression in aggregated primary embryonic pluripotent cells (Figure 2c,d; Video 2), single cell-derived clones started to express GFP at about 16 hr (Video 3)
claims.evidence: This is an observation from time-lapse imaging shown in Video 3.

claims.claim: The onset of retinal fate is genetically timed and independent of cellular environment.
claims.source: indicating that the onset of retinal fate is genetically timed and independent of cellular environment.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that single cells and aggregates show similar timing of Rx3 expression.

claims.claim: Rx3 expression was initiated in the absence of Matrigel already at day 0, indicating that the acquisition of retinal fate occurs spontaneously and independently of extracellular matrix components.
claims.source: Interestingly, Rx3 expression was initiated also in the absence of Matrigel already at day 0, indicating that the acquisition of retinal fate occurs spontaneously and independently of extracellular matrix components.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from organoids cultured without Matrigel.

claims.claim: Matrigel addition triggered the formation of a neuroepithelium by day 2 and confined GFP-expressing cells to the peripheral region of the organoid.
claims.source: Matrigel addition triggered the formation of a neuroepithelium by day 2 and confined GFP-expressing cells to the peripheral region of the organoid.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 2e.

claims.claim: The formation of a neuroepithelium was clearly dependent on the action of Matrigel.
claims.source: The formation of a neuroepithelium was clearly dependent on the action of Matrigel (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The expression of Rx2, Sox2, and Lhx2 transcription factors in the epithelium of day 2 organoids resembled their expression in the neuroepithelium of OV in the 1 dpf embryo.
claims.source: The expression of these transcription factors in the epithelium of day 2 organoids resembled their expression in the neuroepithelium of OV in the 1 dpf embryo (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), indicating that the aggregates adopted the complex retinal fate.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: All organoids (n = ~1500) from 52 independent experiments formed retinal neuroepithelia, indicating that retinal specification under the established conditions is robust and highly efficient.
claims.source: All organoids (n = ~1500) from 52 independent experiments formed retinal neuroepithelia, indicating that retinal specification under the established conditions is robust and highly efficient.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result demonstrating the efficiency of the protocol.

claims.claim: While heterozygotes Rx3saGFP/+ develop normally and give rise to GFP labeled OVs, homozygous-mutant embryos (Rx3saGFP/saGFP) fail to evaginate the OVs from the lateral wall of the diencephalon.
claims.source: While heterozygotes Rx3saGFP/+ develop normally and give rise to GFP labeled OVs, homozygous-mutant embryos (Rx3saGFP/saGFP) fail to evaginate the OVs from the lateral wall of the diencephalon (Figure 2g, Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from the newly generated Rx3saGFP mutant line shown in Figure 2g and Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: While a retinal neuroepithelium formed in Rx3saGFP/+ (n = 9) organoids by day 2, aggregates derived from individual Rx3-mutant homozygote blastulae (Rx3saGFP/saGFP) (n = 4) did not form a neuroepithelium and aggregates were lacking regular morphology by day 2.
claims.source: While a retinal neuroepithelium formed in Rx3saGFP/+ (n = 9) organoids by day 2, aggregates derived from individual Rx3-mutant homozygote blastulae (Rx3saGFP/saGFP) (n = 4) did not form a neuroepithelium and aggregates were lacking regular morphology by day 2 (Figure 2g)
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 2g.

claims.claim: The formation of retinal neuroepithelium is hard-wired also in the organoid and follows the same developmental program as in vivo, also upon loss-of-function.
claims.source: These data indicate that the formation of retinal neuroepithelium is hard-wired also in the organoid and follows the same developmental program as in vivo, also upon loss-of-function (Loosli et al., 2001; Rembold et al., 2006; Stigloher et al., 2006; Winkler et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Rx3 mutant organoid experiments and supported by citations.

claims.claim: Zebrafish cells aggregated as efficiently as medaka cells and displayed an epithelial organization already by day 1.
claims.source: Zebrafish cells aggregated as efficiently as medaka cells and displayed an epithelial organization already by day 1 (Figure 3b).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 3b.

claims.claim: Aggregates generated from zebrafish embryos formed organoids that started expressing GFP at 9.75 ± 0.21 hpa (n = 15).
claims.source: Aggregates generated from zebrafish embryos formed organoids that started expressing GFP at 9.75 ± 0.21 hpa (n = 15).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claims.claim: The onset of Rx3 expression in zebrafish forming organoids was delayed by 2–3 hr in comparison to the corresponding Rx3::H2B-GFP reporter embryos.
claims.source: As in medaka, the onset of Rx3 expression in the forming organoids was delayed by 2–3 hr in comparison to the corresponding Rx3::H2B-GFP reporter embryos (Figure 3c; Video 4) that started to express GFP at 7.88 ± 0.77 hr (n = 6) after the blastula stage.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from time-lapse imaging experiments shown in Figure 3c and Video 4.

claims.claim: The cells followed their endogenous program consistently and were only delayed by the dissociation/aggregation procedure.
claims.source: The cells followed their endogenous program consistently and were only delayed by the dissociation/aggregation procedure.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the timing data comparing embryos and organoids.

claims.claim: The formation of a neuroepithelium in aggregates reflects the species-specific difference in the relative pace of development.
claims.source: Thus, the formation of a neuroepithelium in aggregates reflects the species-specific difference in the relative pace of development.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing medaka and zebrafish organoid development timing.

claims.claim: Under the established conditions, fish primary embryonic pluripotent cells are guided to differentiate into a retinal neuroepithelium – a feature found over a wide evolutionary distant medaka and zebrafish, indicating a deep conservation of early retinal development irrespective of the embryonic environment.
claims.source: This data shows that under the established conditions, fish primary embryonic pluripotent cells are guided to differentiate into a retinal neuroepithelium – a feature found over a wide evolutionary distant medaka and zebrafish, indicating a deep conservation of early retinal development irrespective of the embryonic environment.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the successful generation of retinal organoids from both medaka and zebrafish.

claims.claim: When organoids were generated by the aggregation of >1000 cells, OV formation was not favored and instead these organoids formed a continuous neuroepithelium on their entire surface.
claims.source: When organoids were generated by the aggregation of 1000–2000 cells (referred to as >1000 cells), the approximate number of cells in a single blastula, OV formation was not favored (Figure 4a) and instead these organoids formed a continuous neuroepithelium on their entire surface.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 4a.

claims.claim: This neuroepithelium expressed retina-specific markers (Rx2 and Rx3::H2B-GFP) all around the surface of organoid indicating the formation of a single retinal anlage.
claims.source: This neuroepithelium expressed retina-specific markers (Rx2 and Rx3::H2B-GFP) all around the surface of organoid (Figure 4a–b) indicating the formation of a single retinal anlage.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 4a-b.

claims.claim: Small organoids (generated by the aggregation of <1000 cells) reproducibly displayed expression of Rx2 and Rx3 only in restricted regions reminiscent of the forming OV in vivo.
claims.source: Interestingly, those organoids ('small organoids', generated by the aggregation of <1000 cells) reproducibly displayed expression of Rx2 and Rx3 only in restricted regions (Figure 4a,b) reminiscent of the forming OV in vivo.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 4a-b.

claims.claim: While organoids generated by aggregation of >1000 cells established a single, uniform, domain of retinal neuroepithelium (n = 35/35), small organoids displayed a more complex and variable morphology, forming one to four isolated OV-like retinal domains (n = 92/123 one domain, n = 27/123 two domains, n = 3/123 three domains, and n = 1/123 four domains).
claims.source: While organoids generated by aggregation of >1000 cells established a single, uniform, domain of retinal neuroepithelium (n = 35/35), small organoids displayed a more complex and variable morphology, forming one to four isolated OV-like retinal domains (n = 92/123 one domain, n = 27/123 two domains, n = 3/123 three domains, and n = 1/123 four domains) (Figure 4c, Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from experiments shown in Figure 4c and supplementary figures.

claims.claim: The size of isolated retinal domains in small organoids (154.5 ± 28.6 μm; n = 56) was reminiscent of the OVs in embryos at 1 dpf (162 ± 10.6 μm; n = 16).
claims.source: The size of these isolated retinal domains in small organoids (154.5 ± 28.6 μm; n = 56) was reminiscent of the OVs in embryos at 1 dpf (162 ± 10.6 μm; n = 16) (Figure 4d).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result comparing organoid and embryo measurements shown in Figure 4d.

claims.claim: Retinal domains formed in small organoids displayed OV-like morphology with specifically localized expression of Rx2 and Otx2 transcription factors, marking prospective retinal and RPE territories respectively.
claims.source: Interestingly, retinal domains formed in small organoids displayed OV-like morphology with specifically localized expression of Rx2 and Otx2 transcription factors, marking prospective retinal and RPE territories respectively (Figure 4e) and indicating further compartmentalization of the organoid-derived OV.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 4e.

claims.claim: Small aggregates also established an Rx2-negative, non-retinal domain, expressing the general neuronal marker Sox2 and the forebrain marker Otx2, strongly indicating that the neighboring tissue adopted anterior neuronal identity.
claims.source: Besides the retinal tissue, small aggregates also established an Rx2-negative, non-retinal domain, expressing the general neuronal marker Sox2 (Pevny and Placzek, 2005; Wegner and Stolt, 2005) and the forebrain marker Otx2 (Acampora et al., 1995; Simeone et al., 1993; Tian et al., 2002), strongly indicating that the neighboring tissue adopted anterior neuronal identity (Figure 4f).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 4f and supported by citations.

claims.claim: In a fraction (22%) of organoids, retinal and non-retinal domains showed an arrangement, resembling a 'head with two eyes' (n = 27/123).
claims.source: In a fraction (22%) of organoids, intriguingly, retinal and non-retinal domains showed an arrangement, resembling a 'head with two eyes' (n = 27/123) (Figure 4e–f, Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from experiments shown in Figure 4e-f and supplementary figures.

claims.claim: At the initial time point (24 hpa), GFP-positive cells were distributed throughout the whole volume of the organoid indicating that cells acquired retinal identity individually.
claims.source: At the initial time point (24 hpa), GFP-positive cells were distributed throughout the whole volume of the organoid indicating that cells acquired retinal identity individually.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from live imaging shown in Figure 5a.

claims.claim: Single cell tracking and analysis of cell displacement showed that initially cells behaved as freely diffusing particles.
claims.source: Single cell tracking and analysis of cell displacement showed that initially cells behaved as freely diffusing particles (Figure 5b).
claims.evidence: This is an analysis result from live imaging shown in Figure 5b.

claims.claim: This behavior changed at about 34 hpa, when GFP-positive cells showed directed migration – non-linear growth of mean squared displacement – with an estimated speed of 0.413–0.479 μm/min resulting in the morphogenesis of the OV-like structures by 40 hpa.
claims.source: This behavior changed at about 34 hpa, when GFP-positive cells showed directed migration – non-linear growth of mean squared displacement – with an estimated speed of 0.413–0.479 μm/min resulting in the morphogenesis of the OV-like structures by 40 hpa (Figure 5a,b; Video 5).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative analysis result from live imaging shown in Figure 5a-b and Video 5.

claims.claim: 51% of the Rx3-expressing cells were moving from the center to the periphery (outward) of the organoid and contributed to the formation of the OV.
claims.source: Directionality analysis of single cell tracks (Figure 5c) showed that 51% of the Rx3-expressing cells were moving from the center to the periphery (outward) of the organoid and contributed to the formation of the OV (see dark blue, red, orange, and yellow tracks in Figure 5a).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative analysis result from live imaging shown in Figure 5c.

claims.claim: About 49% of the initially laterally located cells moved in the opposite direction – toward the interior of the organoid (inward).
claims.source: About 49% of the initially laterally located cells moved in the opposite direction – toward the interior of the organoid (inward) (light green track in Figure 5a).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative analysis result from live imaging shown in Figure 5a.

claims.claim: These outward- and inward-directed cell movements were highly reminiscent of the migratory behavior of Rx3-expressing cells during OV formation in medaka fish.
claims.source: These outward- and inward-directed cell movements were highly reminiscent of the migratory behavior of Rx3-expressing cells during OV formation in medaka fish (Rembold et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This is a comparison to in vivo behavior supported by a citation.

claims.claim: The cell behavior in fish organoids closely recapitulates the corresponding behavior during development in vivo.
claims.source: Altogether these results show that the cell behavior in fish organoids closely recapitulates the corresponding behavior during development in vivo.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cell tracking analysis.

claims.claim: The organization of retina-committed cells into the OV neuroepithelium is strictly dependent on the presence of extracellular matrix proteins.
claims.source: It is worth mentioning that the organization of retina-committed cells into the OV neuroepithelium is strictly dependent on the presence of extracellular matrix proteins as Rx3-expressing cells attempt but fail to form OV structures in the absence of Matrigel (Video 7).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Video 7.

claims.claim: Laminin-1 (the main component of the Matrigel) is highly enriched specifically at the basal surface of the forming OV and has been reported to play an essential role in cell polarization and maintenance of neuroepithelial cell morphology during OV evagination.
claims.source: Consistently, laminin-1 (the main component of the Matrigel) is highly enriched specifically at the basal surface of the forming OV and has been reported to play an essential role in cell polarization and maintenance of neuroepithelial cell morphology during OV evagination (Ivanovitch et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claims.claim: Day 3 organoids generated from Atoh7::GFP blastulae showed specific morphology with EGFP-negative non-retinal and EGFP-expressing retinal domains, indicating that the retinal differentiation program was successfully initiated.
claims.source: Day 3 organoids generated from Atoh7::GFP blastulae (generated by the aggregation of <1000 cells) showed specific morphology with EGFP-negative non-retinal and EGFP-expressing retinal domains (Figure 6b; Video 8), indicating that the retinal differentiation program was successfully initiated.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 6b and Video 8.

claims.claim: Non-retinal regions proceeded through the process of neuronal differentiation as indicated by expression of HuC/D, a marker of early post-mitotic neurons.
claims.source: Furthermore, non-retinal regions proceeded through the process of neuronal differentiation as indicated by expression of HuC/D (Figure 6c; Video 8), a marker of early post-mitotic neurons (Good, 1995; Kim et al., 1996; Park et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 6c and Video 8, supported by citations.

claims.claim: Retinal domains of day 4 organoids consisted of differentiating retinal neurons organized in multiple layers of cells differentiating toward amacrine and ganglion (expressing HuC/D), photoreceptor and bipolar (expressing Otx2), as well as horizontal (expressing Prox1) cell lineages.
claims.source: Furthermore, retinal domains of day 4 organoids consisted of differentiating retinal neurons organized in multiple layers of cells differentiating toward amacrine and ganglion (expressing HuC/D) (Kay et al., 2001; Link et al., 2000; Park et al., 2000), photoreceptor and bipolar (expressing Otx2) (Fossat et al., 2007; Glubrecht et al., 2009; Koike et al., 2007; Nishida et al., 2003), as well as horizontal (expressing Prox1) (Dyer et al., 2003) cell lineages (Figure 6d).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 6d, supported by citations.

claims.claim: The arrangement of the respective cellular layers was inverted when compared to normal retinal organization.
claims.source: Interestingly, the arrangement of the respective cellular layers was inverted when compared to normal retinal organization (Figure 6e).
claims.evidence: This is an observation shown in Figure 6e.

claims.claim: This can be attributed to the morphological differences, particularly the OV to optic cup transition, between retinal morphogenesis in vivo and organoid.
claims.source: This can be attributed to the morphological differences, particularly the OV to optic cup transition, between retinal morphogenesis in vivo and organoid.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the inverted layer arrangement.

claims.claim: In organoids, retinal differentiation is initiated without the optic cup formation, most probably leading to the inverted retinal organization.
claims.source: In organoids, retinal differentiation is initiated without the optic cup formation, most probably leading to the inverted retinal organization.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the inverted layer arrangement.

claims.claim: Organoids generated by the aggregation of >1000 cells, which form retinal neuroepithelium around entire organoid surface, proceed through the process of retinal differentiation as well.
claims.source: Organoids generated by the aggregation of >1000 cells, which form retinal neuroepithelium around entire organoid surface, proceed through the process of retinal differentiation as well (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), suggesting that the OV formation is not a prerequisite for the retinal differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: None of the organoids analyzed between day 3 and day 4 (n = 88) showed significant level of pigmentation, the hallmark of RPE differentiation.
claims.source: Although the organoid-derived OVs compartmentalize to prospective retinal and RPE domains by day 2 (Figure 4e), none of the organoids analyzed between day 3 and day 4 (n = 88, data not shown) showed significant level of pigmentation, the hallmark of RPE differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative observation from experiments.

claims.claim: RPE fate was not favored under the established culture conditions.
claims.source: This indicates that, similarly to human and mouse retinal organoid cultures (Eiraku et al., 2011; Kuwahara et al., 2015; Nakano et al., 2012), RPE fate was not favored under the established culture conditions.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lack of pigmentation and supported by citations to similar findings in mammalian organoids.

claims.claim: RPE fate determination in vivo, as well as in retinal organoids, is promoted by the activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway.
claims.source: Previous studies showed that RPE fate determination in vivo, as well as in retinal organoids, is promoted by the activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway (Eiraku et al., 2011; Fujimura et al., 2009; Kuwahara et al., 2015; Nakano et al., 2012; Westenskow et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claims.claim: Compared to control (DMSO-treated) organoids, CHIR-99021-treated day 2 organoids showed a RPE-specific Otx2 expression on the expense of the retina-specific Rx2 expression.
claims.source: Compared to control (DMSO-treated) organoids, CHIR-99021-treated day 2 organoids showed a RPE-specific Otx2 expression on the expense of the retina-specific Rx2 expression (Figure 6—figure supplement 2b).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2b.

claims.claim: By day 4, retinal domains in CHIR-99021-treated organoids (13/13) became pigmented with most cells expressing Otx2, demonstrating that those cells acquired RPE fate.
claims.source: By day 4, retinal domains in treated organoids (13/13) became pigmented with most cells expressing Otx2 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2c), demonstrating that those cells acquired RPE fate.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2c.

claims.claim: Primary embryonic pluripotent cells derived from blastula-stage fish embryos form aggregates with the retinal differentiation potential.
claims.source: Taken together, our findings show that primary embryonic pluripotent cells derived from blastula-stage fish embryos form aggregates with the retinal differentiation potential.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the experimental findings.

claims.claim: By adjusting numbers of aggregating cells and the addition of Matrigel, these aggregates are efficiently directed to the retinal fate, the OV morphogenesis, and the retinal differentiation.
claims.source: By adjusting numbers of aggregating cells and the addition of Matrigel, these aggregates are efficiently directed to the retinal fate, the OV morphogenesis, and the retinal differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the experimental findings.

claims.claim: Human retinal organoids take the longest time to develop.
claims.source: While human retinal organoids are the most desired, they also take the longest time to develop and their systematic analysis is limited by technical challenges in genetic manipulations and, last not least, by the lack of direct comparison to the in vivo biological processes.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a limitation of human retinal organoids in the Discussion.

claims.claim: Fish blastula-derived cells have been used to generate ES cultures.
claims.source: Although fish blastula-derived cells have been used to generate ES cultures (Ho et al., 2014; Hong et al., 1998; Hong et al., 1996; Peng et al., 2019; Robles et al., 2011; Yi et al., 2010), our current understanding of their ability to differentiate and assemble into tissues is very limited.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claims.claim: Zebrafish blastula explants have been found to form polarized aggregates capable of specification of all three germ layers.
claims.source: Zebrafish blastula explants have been found to form polarized aggregates capable of specification of all three germ layers (Fulton et al., 2020; Schauer et al., 2020), resembling mammalian ES cell-derived gastruloids (Beccari et al., 2018; van den Brink et al., 2014; Moris et al., 2020; Turner et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claims.claim: Fish primary ES cells have been directed to differentiate to cardiomyocytes forming beating cell sheets with contractile kinetics and electrophysiological features when cultured under defined chemical and mechanical conditions.
claims.source: Besides that, fish primary ES cells have been directed to differentiate to cardiomyocytes forming beating cell sheets with contractile kinetics and electrophysiological features when cultured under defined chemical and mechanical conditions (Xiao et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claims.claim: Under no condition reported so far, fish-derived 3D in vitro cultures have formed highly organized neural structures.
claims.source: However, under no condition reported so far, fish-derived 3D in vitro cultures have formed highly organized neural structures.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a gap in the literature that the current study addresses.

claims.claim: Inter-species blastula cell transplantation experiments between zebrafish and medaka result in ectopic retina formation composed exclusively of donor cells.
claims.source: In addition, inter-species blastula cell transplantation experiments between zebrafish and medaka result in ectopic retina formation composed exclusively of donor cells (Fuhrmann et al., 2020), further reflecting the intrinsic tendency of primary embryonic pluripotent cells to form retinal structures.
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claims.claim: Retinal fate specification in fish-derived organoids is executed spontaneously.
claims.source: Our results show that retinal fate specification in fish-derived organoids is executed spontaneously.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings showing Rx3 expression without external induction.

claims.claim: The starting size (cell number) of the initial aggregate crucially impacts on the morphogenesis of the resulting organoid.
claims.source: We found that the starting size (cell number) of the initial aggregate crucially impacts on the morphogenesis of the resulting organoid.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from experiments comparing organoids from different cell numbers.

claims.claim: The 'classical' reaction-diffusion model of pattern formation predicts that the number of repeating patterns – OVs – will increase proportionally with tissue size.
claims.source: This appeared counterintuitive, since the 'classical' reaction-diffusion model of pattern formation (Meinhardt, 2012; Turing, 1952) predicts that the number of repeating patterns – OVs – will increase proportionally with tissue size.
claims.evidence: This is a reference to established theory supported by citations.

claims.claim: For fish retinal organoids, the effect is inverted, offering fish retinal organoids as a model to address alternative pattering scenarios.
claims.source: For fish retinal organoids, the effect is however inverted, offering fish retinal organoids as a model to address alternative pattering scenarios.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that larger aggregates form fewer OVs.

claims.claim: Re-aggregation of dissociated fish primary pluripotent cells was fast (about 2–3 hr) and highly efficient (100%) when derived from blastula-stage embryos.
claims.source: Remarkably, re-aggregation of dissociated fish primary pluripotent cells was fast (about 2–3 hr) and highly efficient (100%) when derived from blastula-stage embryos.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from experiments.

claims.claim: With OV formation by day 2 and the onset of differentiation by day 3, fish organoids proceed through development almost 10 times faster than their murine counterparts.
claims.source: With OV formation by day 2 and the onset of differentiation by day 3, fish organoids proceed through development almost 10 times faster than their murine counterparts (Eiraku et al., 2011; Kuwahara et al., 2015; Nakano et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is a comparison to mammalian organoids supported by citations.

claims.claim: The formation of fish retinal organoids followed the in vivo developmental timing, reflecting the difference in relative speed of development of the corresponding species.
claims.source: The formation of fish retinal organoids followed the in vivo developmental timing, reflecting the difference in relative speed of development of the corresponding species.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing medaka and zebrafish organoid development.

claims.claim: This rapid development in combination with the ease of highly efficient genome editing, small size, and full transparency granting direct comparison to in vivo processes, pose fish-derived organoids as a rapid and efficient prototyping platform for systematic drug tests in disease models.
claims.source: This rapid development in combination with the ease of highly efficient genome editing (Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018; Prykhozhij and Berman, 2018; Stemmer et al., 2015), small size, and full transparency granting direct comparison to in vivo processes, pose fish-derived organoids as a rapid and efficient prototyping platform for systematic drug tests in disease models, which then can be translated to more demanding mammalian systems.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion about the potential applications of fish organoids, supported by citations.

claims.claim: In mammalian eye development, paralleled in mouse and human retinal organoid cultures, the OV is formed by a set of coordinated collective epithelial cell movements driving vesicle evagination from the initially formed neuroepithelium.
claims.source: In mammalian eye development, paralleled in mouse and human retinal organoid cultures, the OV is formed by a set of coordinated collective epithelial cell movements driving vesicle evagination from the initially formed neuroepithelium (Chauhan et al., 2015; Eiraku et al., 2011; Martinez-Morales et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claims.claim: In teleosts, OV formation is driven by the individual migration of Rx3-expressing retinal progenitor cells.

claims.claim: The comparison of organoids derived from a wide range of evolutionarily diverse species provides the opportunity to systematically address and distinguish intrinsic and extrinsic constraints contributing to self-organization and organ morphogenesis.
claims.source: The comparison of organoids derived from a wide range of evolutionarily diverse species provides the opportunity to systematically address and distinguish intrinsic and extrinsic constraints contributing to self-organization and organ morphogenesis, and to ultimately tackle the question of the 'conservation' of cellular self-organization, a feature that has apparently not been selected for in evolution.
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the potential of comparative organoid studies.

results.result: Fish blastula-stage cells efficiently aggregate with 100% success rate (n=~1500 from 54 experiments), but this capacity is restricted to the blastula stage (1000-2000 cells), with earlier stages failing to form stable aggregates. Re-aggregation is fast (2-3 hours) and highly efficient.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C13 and C79 provide consistent quantitative evidence with large sample sizes (n=~1500) demonstrating efficient aggregation restricted to blastula stage. The timing and efficiency data are well-documented with appropriate controls showing earlier stages fail to aggregate (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).

results.result: After Matrigel addition at day 1, aggregates form organized neuroepithelium by day 2, with peripheral cells expressing neuroepithelial markers (N-cadherin, acetylated tubulin). Neuroepithelium formation is dependent on Matrigel.
results.evaluation: Claims C14-C15 and C24-C25 are supported by immunostaining data (Figure 1d, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 2) showing marker expression and morphological organization. The Matrigel dependency is demonstrated by direct comparison experiments with and without Matrigel.

results.result: All organoids (n=~1500 from 52 experiments) efficiently acquire retinal fate, with Rx3::H2B-GFP expression starting at 15.5±0.36 hpa in organoids versus 13.5±1.03 hr in embryos, showing a 2-3 hour delay corresponding to re-aggregation time.
results.evaluation: Claims C16-C19 and C27 provide robust quantitative data with large sample sizes and statistical analysis. The timing comparison between organoids and embryos is well-controlled, and the 100% efficiency across ~1500 organoids demonstrates reproducibility and robustness of the protocol.

results.result: Individual blastula-stage cells autonomously acquire retinal fate, with single cell-derived clones expressing GFP at ~16 hr, similar to aggregated cells. Rx3 expression initiates spontaneously without Matrigel, indicating retinal fate acquisition is genetically timed and independent of cellular environment or extracellular matrix.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C23 are supported by single-cell culture experiments (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Video 3) and Matrigel-free culture data. The similar timing between single cells and aggregates provides strong evidence for cell-autonomous, genetically-timed fate specification.

results.result: Day 2 organoids express retinal transcription factors (Rx2, Sox2, Lhx2) in patterns resembling the optic vesicle neuroepithelium of 1 dpf embryos.
results.evaluation: Claim C26 is supported by immunostaining data (Figure 2—figure supplement 3) showing comparable expression patterns between organoids and embryos for multiple retinal markers, indicating complex retinal fate adoption.

results.result: Rx3saGFP homozygous mutant embryos fail to evaginate optic vesicles, and organoids from Rx3saGFP/saGFP blastulae (n=4) fail to form neuroepithelium by day 2, while heterozygotes (n=9) develop normally, demonstrating that organoids follow the same Rx3-dependent developmental program as in vivo.
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C30 are supported by the newly generated Rx3saGFP mutant line data (Figure 2g, Figure 2—figure supplement 4). The genetic loss-of-function experiment provides strong evidence that organoids recapitulate in vivo genetic requirements, though sample size for mutants is small (n=4).

results.result: Zebrafish cells efficiently form organoids with epithelial organization by day 1, expressing Rx3::H2B-GFP at 9.75±0.21 hpa (n=15) versus 7.88±0.77 hr in embryos (n=6), showing the same 2-3 hr delay as medaka. The species-specific developmental timing is preserved in organoids, indicating deep conservation of early retinal development across evolutionarily distant fish species.
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C36 demonstrate successful extension to zebrafish with appropriate sample sizes and timing analysis (Figure 3, Video 4). The preservation of species-specific developmental pace in organoids provides strong evidence for conservation of retinal development programs across species.

results.result: Cell number critically impacts organoid morphogenesis: >1000 cell aggregates form uniform retinal neuroepithelium (n=35/35), while <1000 cell aggregates form 1-4 isolated OV-like domains (n=123 total: 92 one domain, 27 two domains, 3 three domains, 1 four domains). Small organoid OV domains (154.5±28.6 μm, n=56) match embryonic OV size (162±10.6 μm, n=16).
results.evaluation: Claims C37-C41 and C76 provide comprehensive quantitative data with appropriate sample sizes showing clear cell number-dependent morphological outcomes (Figure 4a-d). The size measurements demonstrate organoid OVs match in vivo dimensions. However, the inverse relationship with classical reaction-diffusion models (C77-C78) requires further mechanistic investigation.

results.result: Small organoids form OV-like structures with compartmentalized Rx2+ retinal and Otx2+ RPE territories, plus Rx2-negative/Sox2+/Otx2+ non-retinal domains indicating anterior neuronal identity. 22% of organoids (n=27/123) show 'head with two eyes' arrangement.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C44 are supported by immunostaining data (Figure 4e-f, supplementary figures) showing appropriate marker expression patterns. The quantification of organoid arrangements provides clear evidence for complex tissue organization, though the mechanisms driving this patterning remain unclear.

results.result: Live imaging reveals OV morphogenesis in organoids involves initial random cell distribution (24 hpa), followed by directed migration starting at 34 hpa (0.413-0.479 μm/min). 51% of Rx3+ cells move outward (center to periphery) and 49% move inward, recapitulating the individual cell migration mechanism observed during in vivo teleost OV formation, indicating this is a 'hard-wired' feature independent of embryonic environment.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C51 and C85-C86 are supported by detailed cell tracking analysis (Figure 5, Videos 5-6) with quantitative measurements (n=4600 tracks). The comparison to published in vivo data (Rembold et al., 2006) and demonstration of similar behavior across different organoid types provides strong evidence for conservation of cellular mechanisms.

results.result: OV neuroepithelium organization strictly depends on extracellular matrix proteins, as Rx3+ cells fail to form OV structures without Matrigel. This is consistent with laminin-1's reported role in cell polarization and neuroepithelial morphology during OV evagination.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C53 are supported by Video 7 showing failed OV formation without Matrigel, and C53 is supported by citation to prior work (Ivanovitch et al., 2013). The dependency on extracellular matrix is clearly demonstrated experimentally.

results.result: Day 3 organoids initiate retinal differentiation with Atoh7::EGFP+ retinal domains and HuC/D+ non-retinal neuronal differentiation. By day 4, organoids contain multiple retinal cell layers expressing markers for amacrine/ganglion (HuC/D), photoreceptor/bipolar (Otx2), and horizontal (Prox1) cells. Both >1000 and <1000 cell organoids undergo differentiation, indicating OV formation is not required for retinal differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C56 and C60 are supported by marker expression data (Figure 6, Video 8, Figure 6—figure supplement 1) with appropriate citations for marker specificity. The demonstration of differentiation in both organoid types provides evidence that morphogenesis and differentiation can be partially uncoupled.

results.result: Organoid retinal layers show inverted arrangement compared to normal retinal organization, attributed to morphological differences in OV to optic cup transition and initiation of differentiation without optic cup formation.
results.evaluation: Claim C57 is supported by observation (Figure 6e), but C58-C59 are speculative interpretations without direct experimental evidence. The proposed mechanism for inverted organization requires further investigation to determine causality.

results.result: Organoids lack RPE pigmentation under standard conditions (n=88 analyzed), but CHIR-99021 treatment (GSK3β inhibitor activating Wnt/β-catenin) induces RPE fate, with day 2 organoids showing RPE-specific Otx2 expression and day 4 organoids (13/13) showing pigmentation and Otx2 expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C65 are supported by experimental data (Figure 6—figure supplement 2) showing lack of pigmentation in controls and successful RPE induction with CHIR-99021 (100% efficiency, n=13/13). The result is consistent with cited mammalian organoid studies and known Wnt/β-catenin pathway role in RPE specification.

results.result: Primary embryonic pluripotent cells from medaka and zebrafish efficiently assemble into retinal organoids that execute key steps of eye development (specification, morphogenesis, differentiation) within 4 days. Cell number and genetic factors (e.g., Rx3) critically impact morphological outcomes, which reflect in vivo situations.
results.evaluation: This summary result integrates multiple major findings (C2-C4, C66-C67) that are each well-supported by extensive experimental data throughout the manuscript. The claims represent the core conclusions of the study with robust evidence from both medaka and zebrafish systems.

results.result: Fish organoids develop ~10 times faster than murine counterparts (OV by day 2, differentiation by day 3), following species-specific in vivo developmental timing. Combined with efficient genome editing, small size, and transparency, fish organoids offer a rapid prototyping platform for drug testing in disease models.
results.evaluation: Claims C80-C81 are supported by timing data and citations to mammalian studies. However, C82's claim about drug testing applications is speculative and represents future potential rather than demonstrated capability. The comparison to mammalian systems is valid but the translational applications remain to be proven.

results.result: Fish retinal organoids show inverted relationship to classical reaction-diffusion models, with larger aggregates forming fewer OV patterns rather than more, offering a model to address alternative patterning scenarios.
results.evaluation: Claims C77-C78 correctly cite classical theory but the mechanistic explanation for the inverted pattern remains unclear. While the observation is well-documented (C40), the claim that this offers insight into alternative patterning scenarios is speculative without further mechanistic investigation.

results.result: Mammalian OV formation involves coordinated collective epithelial cell movements, while teleost OV formation is driven by individual migration of Rx3+ retinal progenitor cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C84 are well-supported by citations to prior research. These represent established knowledge from the literature that provides context for interpreting the organoid findings.

results.result: In vertebrates, retinal development initiates during neurulation with eye field specification by transcription factors (Rx, Lhx2, Pax6, Six3, Otx2), followed by optic vesicle formation. Rx3 is crucial for OV evagination, with Rx3-null mutants failing to form OVs and Rx3-deficient cells excluded from OV domains.
results.evaluation: Claims C5-C10 represent well-established background knowledge supported by multiple citations to prior research. These provide essential context for the study but are not novel findings.

results.result: Fish blastula-derived cells have been used for ES cultures and can form polarized aggregates with three germ layers or differentiate to cardiomyocytes, but have not previously formed highly organized neural structures.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C72 are supported by citations to prior work and accurately describe the state of the field before this study. C72 identifies the gap that the current work addresses.

results.result: Inter-species blastula cell transplantation between zebrafish and medaka results in ectopic retina formation from donor cells, and retinal fate specification in fish organoids occurs spontaneously without external induction.
results.evaluation: Claim C74 is supported by citation to prior work. Claim C75 is supported by experimental data showing Rx3 expression without external induction factors (C23). Together these support the intrinsic tendency of fish pluripotent cells to form retinal structures.

results.result: Mammalian organoids are limited by long developmental time, variable success, and lack of direct in vivo comparison. Human retinal organoids take the longest time to develop.
results.evaluation: Claims C1 and C68 represent established limitations of mammalian organoid systems that motivate the development of fish organoid models. These are general knowledge claims that provide rationale for the study.

results.result: Selection acts only on development in embryonic context. Organoid resemblance to organs may indicate environment-independent self-organizing capacity. Comparative organoid studies across species could distinguish intrinsic versus extrinsic constraints on morphogenesis and address 'conservation' of cellular self-organization.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C89 are speculative theoretical interpretations about evolutionary and developmental principles. While thought-provoking, these represent hypotheses rather than demonstrated findings. The ideas require substantial future work to test experimentally.
